LanguageData.RHAH_Suiyin.label: Suiyin
LanguageData.RHAH_Suiyin.description:
Suiyin is a princess of the ratkin kingdom, raised in the court. She slipped out of the palace to play and saw the common quarter on the other side of one wall. The ratkin there were filthy. Their eyes were dull. They did work their skeleton-thin bodies could not carry. Garbage, refuse, and waste filled the ground and the ditches. People fought to the death over a mouthful of food. The maids had told her, since she was small, that the world outside was bright, and that every rat was rich, kind, and generous. What she found was drugs, alcohol, and a silence like a graveyard.

She ran back and kept asking her parents. They said, "Why did you sneak out again?" "Do not leave the palace. The world outside is false." "Do not believe what you see." Then they locked her in.

On this side of the wall: feasting, money, and power. Everyone was rich or noble. Everyone wore a mask. The floors were gold or jade, and the air smelled of luxury. On the other side: suffering and despair. People were dying or already hurt. Their eyes were empty. Their breath stank of rot. Staying alive took everything they had.

One day she climbed a tree over the palace wall and walked into the common quarter. Her fine clothes did not belong there. She passed the working ratkin slowly, afraid that coming too close would make one of them fall. She could do nothing. She stepped on a fresh corpse and did not notice. It felt no different from the ground.

How does kindness actually get done? Nobles and the rich prayed to the rat god almost every day. They asked for money, and for their families. Who actually lived by the teaching to spread love?

A hand stopped her. The man had red hair and a calm face. An unlit cigarette hung from his left hand. His purple coat bore a smiling face, as if her questions were a joke. "Come on. Let's see what an archotech will do." He smiled without much effort and held out his right hand. Suiyin looked him in the eye and put her right hand in his.

She records the ratkin, famines, and plagues your colony meets, then answers what has already happened. She does not decide for you.

Her pace is close to Randy's. Ratkin famine sits on top of that, so the game is harder. When she trusts this colony, major threats come less often. When she does not, they come more often.
